_comment: Drafted 2026-09-04 from public comparison material, before starting at Greenhouse. These are a starting point, NOT official positioning. Greenhouse enablement will have real cards with real win/loss data behind them; when they conflict, theirs win. Every card carries a 'theyWin' section on purpose: a prospect evaluating Ashby has probably already read the Ashby marketing site, and a rep who cannot name a competitor's genuine strength is not credible for the rest of the call.
_wiring: handoff.mjs pulls the card matching the detected ATS. Deliberately NOT wired into brief.mjs, because competitive positioning is internal and does not belong in anything a prospect reads.

ashby.name: Ashby
ashby.profile: Data-driven, engineering-led startups and scale-ups, roughly 50 to 1,000 employees. Series A through late growth. Stands up fast.
theyChoseItBecause: Analytics. Interactive exploration, custom reports on any field, drill-down from dashboard to individual candidate. Users describe it as replacing a separate BI tool.
One platform for ATS, CRM, scheduling and analytics rather than four contracts.
Fast to implement, which matters to a small talent team with no ops headcount.
whereGreenhouseWins: Structured hiring as a method, not a feature. Interview kits, competency-based scorecards, defined evaluation criteria applied consistently across every candidate.
Scorecard depth. Ashby users report competency data does not pull together well across interviews, so comparing two candidates on the same competency is harder than it should be.
Scale and process complexity. Greenhouse fits larger organisations running multi-stage hiring with a dedicated recruiting team; Ashby is built for leaner teams.
The interviewer experience. Structured kits mean a hiring manager who has never interviewed for this role still runs a consistent loop.
whereTheyWin: Reporting, plainly. Greenhouse's reporting is functional but limited, and custom reporting means exporting to an external tool. Do not pretend otherwise, they will have tested both.
Ashby sells a standalone analytics product that layers on top of Greenhouse. If reporting is their only complaint, that is a real option and pretending it is not costs you credibility.
questionsThatOpenIt: When two interviewers score the same candidate differently, how do you resolve it today?
How much of your interview process lives in the tool versus in someone's head?
Who builds your reports, and how long does a new one take?
doNotSay: That Ashby has no analytics. It is their strongest area and the claim ends the call.
That they are a startup tool. They serve real scale-ups and the prospect knows it.

lever.name: Lever
lever.profile: ATS plus CRM in one (LeverTRM). Teams focused on talent pooling, nurture campaigns and long-term candidate relationships.
theyChoseItBecause: The CRM half. Sourcing-heavy teams that nurture passive candidates over months.
Simplicity. Easier to adopt than an enterprise system.
One vendor for pipeline and nurture.
whereGreenhouseWins: Workflow control. Power users moving from Greenhouse find Lever rigid; scheduling, job templates and approval workflows are commonly called out as inflexible.
Reporting without a paid add-on. Lever's advanced analytics is an upsell, and teams needing executive dashboards or multi-dimensional analysis hit walls.
Approval workflows and multi-location posting, which are recurring reasons teams outgrow Lever.
Structured hiring depth. Lever's strength is relationship management, not interview rigour.
whereTheyWin: Native candidate nurture. If they run genuine long-cycle sourcing campaigns, that is real and Greenhouse's CRM is a different shape.
Perceived simplicity. Some teams do not want the process discipline Greenhouse asks for.
questionsThatOpenIt: What happens when you need a report nobody built before?
How many approval steps does a new req go through, and where does it get stuck?
If you post one role across four locations, how many records is that?
doNotSay: That Lever has no CRM. It is the product's whole identity.

workday.name: Workday Recruiting
workday.profile: The recruiting module inside an HCM suite. Usually already bought at the CHRO or CFO level for reasons that have nothing to do with recruiting.
theyChoseItBecause: It came with the HCM. Nobody selected it on recruiting merit.
One system of record for employee data, and IT prefers one vendor.
whereGreenhouseWins: This is a co-existence pitch, not a rip-and-replace. Many Workday shops run a best-of-breed front end (Greenhouse, iCIMS, SmartRecruiters) integrated into Workday, keeping the HCM and giving recruiters a tool built for recruiting.
Recruiting-specific depth. Workday has historically lagged dedicated ATS platforms; its candidate experience and recruiting analytics are described as functional but not best-in-class.
Recruiter experience. The daily user is a recruiter, and that is who Greenhouse is designed for.
Speed of change. A workflow change in Workday is a project.
whereTheyWin: Single system of record. Data flows to payroll and HRIS without an integration, and that is genuinely valuable to the person who signed the Workday contract.
They are not going to rip out Workday. Do not ask them to.
questionsThatOpenIt: Who actually lives in the system all day, and did they get a vote?
When you need a change to a hiring workflow, who do you ask and how long does it take?
Are you open to keeping Workday as the system of record and putting something purpose-built in front of it?
doNotSay: Anything that sounds like replacing Workday. It is a six-figure contract someone senior defended.
That their data is a mess. You do not know that.

icims.name: iCIMS
icims.profile: Enterprise ATS built for IT-managed deployments. Strong configurability, high complexity. Contracts commonly $30k to $100k+.
theyChoseItBecause: It scales to very large, very complex hiring operations.
whereGreenhouseWins: Recruiter usability. iCIMS's depth comes with interface complexity, and recruiters commonly find it less intuitive than mid-market alternatives.
Time to change anything. iCIMS was architected for IT-managed deployment, so admin-heavy configuration is required for every workflow change.
Adoption. A system recruiters avoid produces bad data regardless of how configurable it is.
whereTheyWin: Genuine enterprise compliance and configurability. If they are regulated and highly complex, iCIMS earns its place.
Scale. At very large hiring volumes it is a serious product.
questionsThatOpenIt: How long does a workflow change take from asking to live?
What percentage of your recruiters use it the way it was configured?
Where does your team keep the spreadsheets that work around it?
doNotSay: That iCIMS is legacy. It is actively developed and the claim reads as lazy.

smartrecruiters.name: SmartRecruiters
smartrecruiters.profile: Enterprise-leaning platform with a strong marketplace and a broad feature surface. Common in Europe and in high-volume hiring.
whereGreenhouseWins: Structured hiring method and interview kit depth.
Focus. A narrower product used well beats a broad one used partially.
The interviewer experience, which is where structured hiring compounds.
whereTheyWin: Marketplace breadth and international job-board distribution.
High-volume hourly hiring, which is a different problem from structured knowledge-worker hiring.
questionsThatOpenIt: Which parts of the platform do you actually use?
How consistent is your interview process between two different hiring managers?

workable.name: Workable
workable.profile: SMB and lower mid-market. Fast setup, broad job-board posting, low price point. Often the first real ATS a company buys.
theyChoseItBecause: Price and speed. It was the obvious step up from a spreadsheet.
Job-board distribution out of the box.
whereGreenhouseWins: This is usually an outgrowing story, not a displacement one. They bought Workable at 40 people and they are now 200.
Structured hiring, scorecards and interview kits, which matter once more than a handful of people interview.
Reporting and process consistency across a real recruiting team.
Approval workflows and multi-stakeholder hiring.
whereTheyWin: Price. Greenhouse costs meaningfully more and you should not pretend the gap is small.
Simplicity for a small team. If they are still under about 50 people, they may genuinely not need Greenhouse yet, and saying so buys you the call in a year.
questionsThatOpenIt: How many people were you when you bought it, and how many are you now?
Who owns making sure two hiring managers run the same process?
What is the thing you keep meaning to fix about hiring but never get to?
doNotSay: That Workable is not a real ATS. It is, and it was the right call when they bought it.

recruitee.name: Recruitee
recruitee.profile: SMB and European mid-market, part of Tellent. Collaborative hiring emphasis, straightforward setup.
theyChoseItBecause: Simple collaborative hiring for small teams.
whereGreenhouseWins: Depth of structured hiring and scorecards.
Scale of recruiting operation and reporting.
US and global enterprise footprint if they are expanding into the States.
whereTheyWin: Simplicity for a team that is not running complex loops.
questionsThatOpenIt: Are you hiring outside Europe yet, and how is that going?
How do you compare two candidates interviewed by different people?

none.name: No ATS detected
none.profile: Either they run no ATS, or they proxy their careers page server-side so the platform is hidden. Check the careers page apply link before assuming greenfield.
theyChoseItBecause: Genuine greenfield: hiring runs on a shared inbox, a spreadsheet and a calendar.
Or they have one and you simply cannot see it from outside.
whereGreenhouseWins: Everything, if it is genuinely greenfield. There is no incumbent to displace and no migration to fear.
The pain is already acute: lost candidates, no audit trail, no idea why anyone dropped out.
Greenfield deals close faster because there is no switching cost argument to win.
whereTheyWin: Free. A spreadsheet costs nothing and the status quo is the hardest competitor there is.
questionsThatOpenIt: Where does a CV live between someone applying and someone reading it?
If I asked why you passed on a candidate three months ago, could you tell me?
Who is the one person who knows where everything is, and what happens when they are away?
doNotSay: That they have no process. They have one, it is just not in software.
